name: Indigo iUSD
oneLiner: iUSD is Indigo Protocol's decentralized synthetic dollar on Cardano, minted against overcollateralized CDP vaults of Cardano-native assets.
collateral: ADA-only collateral in overcollateralized Indigo Protocol CDP vaults; deposited ADA continues earning Cardano staking rewards via CDP Liquid Staking
pegMechanism: Overcollateralized ADA-backed CDP synthetic dollar that tracks the median oracle price of USDC, USDT, and TUSD (fault-tolerant triple-peg). Solvency is maintained by per-iAsset Stability Pools that absorb liquidations of undercollateralized CDPs (Stability Providers paid in ADA collateral plus INDY), plus V2 redemptions (RMR hard peg) and a DAO-set variable interest rate (soft peg). Collateral parameters and MCR are governed by the INDY DAO

mechanismArchetypeReview.rationale: Indigo documents iUSD as an overcollateralized Cardano CDP whose debt is minted against ADA collateral; the Koios policy record anchors the current Cardano implementation boundary used for the implementation date.

oracleRisk.summary: Public docs reviewed for Indigo iUSD do not identify the collateral oracle setup or failure handling.

sources.label: Koios V3 PSM reference output API

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Indigo's V3 documentation, last updated 2026-06-25, describes an iUSD/USDCx Peg Stabilization Module: USDCx-to-iUSD minting and iUSD-to-USDCx redemption. It states that the DAO can enable or disable each direction of a stable pair and that the Indigo Foundation controlled loan redemptions at V3 launch. The official V3 configuration identifies PSM reference output 5a3581c7623683ca7a458f368d215816390c9cdaa8b5748deb7904b571889005#0; a Koios POST to utxo_info on 2026-07-15 returned PlutusV3 script hash 245425bb49411414dca4af8f25097c5a27f923249c0779ffaa2bc5a3, whose serialized validation messages include 'Minting is not enabled' and 'Redeeming is not enabled'. The current iUSD policy reference 8fac023fd9556f66ffdac8cb71879fabd6995480f7ad976213d1e1ee85de75cd#0 is PlutusV2, so the earlier policy was not treated as current PSM source evidence. Cardano documents that ordinary native-token transfers do not execute a policy, and no holder-address blacklist or direct iUSD transfer freeze was established. USDCx terms state that Circle may delay or deny xReserve USDC release and bridge parties may pause the bridge. This establishes possible governed PSM and upstream redemption-route access exposure, not a claim that an issuer can freeze standalone iUSD balances.

The public sources establish the collateral category but do not publish a dated aggregate ADA balance, vault distribution, or liquidation-liquidity reconciliation; the 100% envelope therefore remains an explicit category-level review with unknown current exposure details.

mintAuthority.summary: iUSD is minted on Cardano by opening overcollateralized CDPs in Indigo Protocol against approved Cardano-native collateral; INDY token holders govern collateral onboarding, parameters, and stability mechanisms.

controls.label: Indigo CDP minting validators
controls.capDescription: iUSD (an iAsset) is minted only against overcollateralized Indigo CDP vaults of approved Cardano collateral; supply expands and contracts with collateralized positions and liquidations, not an issuer minter.
controls.evidence: Koios script_info re-verified 2026-07-20: the iUSD minting policy f66d78b4a3cb3d37afa0ec36461e51ecbde00f26c8f0a68f94b69880 is a plutusV2 script (1189 bytes, creation tx 99329591f444f68ed4a33ed664c146fbf278cf9202067974cfa1a26d09a34107, deployed Nov 2022). Cardano minting policies are immutable: the policy hash is the asset identity and its mint rules (overcollateralized CDP validation) cannot be replaced or upgraded for the existing iUSD asset. Indigo docs describe iUSD minted only against overcollateralized CDPs with Stability Pool liquidations.

controls.label: Indigo INDY DAO governance
controls.capDescription: INDY stakers vote on collateral types, CDP risk parameters, and protocol stability mechanisms through Indigo on-chain governance.
controls.evidence: Indigo's official mainnet V3 system parameters (config.indigoprotocol.io) name the on-chain governance surface: GOV_NFT policy 2fccae8bc1c8553a2185b2e77ccdea22f2e1d6e87beb80ef4eaf8cce, poll manager validator 2c64c712d8ea012866a0e52119409992dcbee828b5e89f58b6c13c68, governance execute validator 0e764163b06d954f2dcfecf8d3b257e2bfe3d326d5670e54ca1974ce (this control's address), treasury validator 46ffe1d162ef5c1c4d4c0b92eb410e8148c59c547952ebac39622abd, UPGRADE token ca72f111cc130ac311259181e0720516c044cee30704706a0299c2a8, and VERSION_RECORD token d626ddf398b0bca6e112cf0b78c8124b989a6ca4e7c0dfe8c18c7c2e. Koios script_info on 2026-07-20 confirmed all six resolve to live on-chain scripts (plutusV2 token policies, plutusV3 validators). INDY stakers vote through the poll manager; execution flows through the gov-execute validator against the treasury. Governance controls parameters and validator versions via the upgrade-token mechanism but cannot replace the immutable iUSD minting policy.

review.evidence: 2026-07-20 re-review. Koios script_info confirms the iUSD minting policy f66d78b4a3cb3d37afa0ec36461e51ecbde00f26c8f0a68f94b69880 is a plutusV2 script (1189 bytes, creation tx 99329591f444f68ed4a33ed664c146fbf278cf9202067974cfa1a26d09a34107): no privileged owner or minter address, minting enforced by CDP collateral logic, and immutable — Cardano policy hashes permanently bind the script, so neither the DAO nor any admin can upgrade or replace the iUSD minting validator for the existing asset. The INDY DAO on-chain governance surface named in Indigo's official mainnet V3 system parameters (GOV_NFT 2fccae8b..., poll manager 2c64c712..., gov execute 0e764163..., treasury 46ffe1d1..., UPGRADE ca72f111..., VERSION_RECORD d626ddf3...) was verified on-chain via Koios: all six scripts exist (plutusV2/plutusV3). Governance authority is therefore parameter-and-version control through the upgrade-token mechanism, not mint authority over iUSD. Economic cap semantics: bounded — iUSD mints only against overcollateralized CDP collateral.
